lessons.title: L'hiver arrive!
lessons.oneGoal: Students understand that 'hiver' means winter and can identify winter weather signs
lessons.openingConnection: Look outside! What do you notice about the weather? Today we learn about 'hiver'!

mainActivity.description: Winter weather exploration with sensory experiences
activities: Show winter weather photos and introduce 'hiver' with shivering gesture
Practice 'froid' with arms hugging self and cold expressions
Explore 'neige' with white paper snow and gentle falling gestures
Winter weather sorting: hot vs cold, summer vs winter pictures
Create classroom winter scene with cotton snow and winter animals
Winter weather walk: observe real winter signs outside or in photos
visualSupports: Large winter weather photo collection showing snow, ice, frost
Temperature gestures (shivering for froid, warm for chaud)
Real winter items to touch: ice cubes, fake snow, winter gloves
Weather sorting cards for hands-on categorization

decisionPoints.question: Are students familiar with seasonal vocabulary?
decisionPoints.ifFamiliar: Build on existing knowledge and add French winter words
decisionPoints.ifNotFamiliar: Start with basic hot/cold concepts before introducing hiver

decisionPoints.question: Do students need visual winter weather supports?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use lots of photos, real ice, cotton snow for tactile experience
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on gestures and movement to represent winter weather

decisionPoints.question: Should I include local winter experiences?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use photos of local winter scenes and weather students recognize
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use general winter images that represent universal winter experiences

whenThingsGoWrong.studentsCold: Move indoors quickly and use warm gestures to teach 'froid'
whenThingsGoWrong.noWinterOutside: Use ice cubes and photos to create winter sensory experience
whenThingsGoWrong.vocabularyOverload: Focus only on 'hiver' and reinforce with lots of repetition

lessons.closing: Students point outside and say 'C'est l'hiver!' while doing shivering gesture
lessons.realWorldConnection: Winter brings changes in weather, clothing, and activities that affect daily life

lessons.title: Que porte-t-on en hiver?
lessons.oneGoal: Students can name 3 winter clothing items in French
lessons.openingConnection: Brrr! It's froid in hiver! What do we put on to stay warm?

mainActivity.description: Winter clothing exploration with dress-up and movement
activities: Review 'froid' and demonstrate need for warm clothes
Introduce 'manteau' with coat-putting-on gesture and real coats
Practice 'mitaines' with hand-warming gesture and mittens to try on
Learn 'tuque' with head-covering gesture and winter hats collection
Winter clothing dress-up fashion show with French vocabulary
Clothing sorting game: winter clothes vs summer clothes
Students draw themselves wearing winter clothes with French labels
visualSupports: Real winter clothing collection for trying on
Clothing gesture cards showing how to wear each item
Before/after pictures: same person in summer vs winter clothes
Cultural winter clothing from different countries

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for clothing vocabulary?
decisionPoints.ifReady: Add all three clothing items and encourage dress-up play
decisionPoints.ifNotReady: Focus on just 'manteau' and let students try on coats

decisionPoints.question: Do students need to touch real winter clothes?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide collection of clean winter items for students to try on
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use pictures and gestures to demonstrate winter clothing

decisionPoints.question: Should I include different cultural winter clothing?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Show winter clothes from different cultures: parkas, scarves, boots styles
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on common local winter clothing students would recognize

materials: Collection of clean winter clothing items

whenThingsGoWrong.clothingTooLarge: Focus on naming rather than wearing, use gestures
whenThingsGoWrong.studentsOverexcited: Calm with quiet clothing naming game using pictures
whenThingsGoWrong.hygienesConcerns: Use clean demonstration items only, no sharing of worn items

lessons.closing: Students model their winter clothing and name one item: 'Je porte mon manteau'
lessons.realWorldConnection: People wear special clothes to stay warm during winter

lessons.title: Activités d'hiver amusantes
lessons.oneGoal: Students can identify winter activities they can do outside
lessons.openingConnection: We have our manteau, mitaines, tuque! Now what can we DO in the neige?

mainActivity.description: Winter activities exploration with movement and imaginative play
activities: Review winter clothing and introduce fun winter activities
Demonstrate 'glisser' with sliding motion and sledding photos
Practice 'patiner' with skating movements and ice skating videos
Explore 'jouer' in winter context: snowball games, snow angels
Winter activity charades: act out activities for others to guess
Create classroom winter playground with activity stations
Students draw their favorite winter activity with French labels
visualSupports: Winter activity photos: sledding, skating, building snowmen, skiing
Movement cards showing how to mime each activity
Video clips of children doing winter activities safely
Activity station signs with pictures and French words

decisionPoints.question: Do students have experience with winter activities?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let students share their experiences and add French vocabulary
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use videos and photos to introduce winter activities concept

decisionPoints.question: Should I focus on activities available locally?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize winter activities students can actually do in their area
decisionPoints.ifNo: Include variety of winter activities from different regions

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for action vocabulary?
decisionPoints.ifReady: Add all three activities with movement and action practice
decisionPoints.ifNotReady: Focus on one activity and practice movement thoroughly

materials: Winter activity photo and video collection
Space for movement and miming activities
Props for activity stations (scarves for skating, pillows for sledding)

whenThingsGoWrong.limitedSpace: Use finger movements and seated gestures for activities
whenThingsGoWrong.studentsFearful: Emphasize safety and fun, show gentle winter activities
whenThingsGoWrong.noWinterExperience: Use imagination and stories to make activities accessible

lessons.closing: Students choose favorite winter activity and demonstrate: 'J'aime glisser!'
lessons.realWorldConnection: Winter offers unique outdoor activities and fun experiences

lessons.title: Animaux en hiver
lessons.oneGoal: Students understand how animals prepare for and survive winter
lessons.openingConnection: We jouer outside in hiver! But what do animals do when it's froid?

mainActivity.description: Animal winter survival exploration with movement and discovery
activities: Introduce winter animal survival as fascinating mystery
Learn about 'ours' with bear gesture and hibernation photos
Explore 'oiseaux' migration with flying movements and bird photos
Practice 'dormir' with sleeping gesture and hibernation concept
Animal winter survival sorting: hibernate, migrate, stay active
Act out animal winter behaviors with movements and sounds
Create winter animal habitat scenes with students as animals
visualSupports: Animal winter survival photos: bears sleeping, birds flying south, deer in snow
Animal movement cards for acting out behaviors
Hibernation den photos and migration maps
Before/after photos: animals in summer vs winter

decisionPoints.question: Are students interested in animal behavior?
decisionPoints.ifInterested: Include detailed animal stories and lots of movement activities
decisionPoints.ifNotInterested: Keep simple with basic vocabulary and gentle animal photos

decisionPoints.question: Do students need animal pictures for support?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use lots of real animal photos and videos of winter behaviors
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on movement and acting out animal winter behaviors

decisionPoints.question: Should I include hibernation concepts?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explain simple hibernation as long winter sleep for some animals
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus just on vocabulary and what animals do differently in winter

materials: Soft materials for hibernation den dramatic play

whenThingsGoWrong.studentsScared: Focus on how clever animals are, not on survival dangers
whenThingsGoWrong.tooComplicated: Simply say animals have special ways to stay warm in winter
whenThingsGoWrong.limitedMovement: Use finger puppets or small movements for animal behaviors

lessons.closing: Students choose animal and show winter behavior: 'L'ours dormir en hiver'
lessons.realWorldConnection: Animals have special ways to survive cold winter weather

lessons.title: Célébrations autour du monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students discover that many cultures celebrate during winter season
lessons.openingConnection: Animals dormir in hiver, but people have special parties! Let's discover célébrations!

mainActivity.description: Global winter celebration exploration with cultural appreciation
activities: Introduce 'célébration' with party gesture and celebration photos
Explore 'lumières' with candles, lights, and bright celebration images
Connect 'famille' to winter celebrations and gathering photos
World tour of winter celebrations: show different cultural celebrations
Light ceremony: demonstrate different ways cultures use lights in winter
Family celebration sharing: students tell about their family traditions
Create celebration collage with diverse cultural winter celebration images
visualSupports: Photos of diverse winter celebrations from around the world
World map showing where different celebrations happen
Real candles, string lights, lanterns (safely demonstrated)
Cultural celebration music and sounds
Family celebration photos representing different traditions

decisionPoints.question: Which cultural celebrations should I include?
decisionPoints.ifInclusive: Show Christmas, Hanukkah, Kwanzaa, Diwali, Chinese New Year, winter solstice
decisionPoints.ifFocused: Choose 3-4 major celebrations and explore them briefly

decisionPoints.question: Do students need visual supports for different traditions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use photos, artifacts, music, and cultural items for each celebration
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on storytelling and discussion about different celebrations

decisionPoints.question: Should I focus on similarities or differences?
decisionPoints.ifSimilarities: Emphasize how all celebrations bring famille together with lumières
decisionPoints.ifDifferences: Celebrate unique traditions and customs from each culture

materials: Safe lighting demonstrations (battery candles, string lights)

whenThingsGoWrong.culturalSensitivity: Present all celebrations as equally beautiful and important
whenThingsGoWrong.overwhelmingChoices: Focus on 2-3 celebrations and explore them gently
whenThingsGoWrong.studentExclusion: Ensure every student's family traditions are valued

lessons.closing: Students point to celebration photo and say: 'C'est une belle célébration!'
lessons.realWorldConnection: Many cultures have special celebrations during winter months

lessons.title: Noël autour du monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore how Christmas is celebrated in different French-speaking countries
lessons.openingConnection: Today we explore one winter célébration: Noël! How is it celebrated around the world?

mainActivity.description: Christmas traditions exploration with French cultural focus
activities: Introduce 'Noël' with celebration gesture and Christmas photos
Explore 'sapin' (Christmas tree) with tree shape and evergreen photos
Learn 'cadeaux' (gifts) with giving gesture and wrapped present photos
Christmas around the world tour: France, Quebec, Africa, Caribbean
Compare Christmas traditions: different trees, foods, gift traditions
Christmas craft: create simple French Christmas decoration
Christmas song: learn simple French Christmas carol with movements
visualSupports: Christmas photos from French-speaking countries
Different types of Christmas trees and decorations
Cultural Christmas foods and traditions photos
Simple French Christmas song with picture supports
Craft materials for cultural Christmas decoration

decisionPoints.question: Should I include diverse Christmas traditions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Show Christmas celebrations from different French-speaking cultures
decisionPoints.ifFocused: Focus on French and French-Canadian Christmas traditions

decisionPoints.question: Do students celebrate Christmas at home?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let students share their family Christmas traditions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Present Christmas as one of many beautiful winter celebrations

decisionPoints.question: How can I be inclusive of all students?
decisionPoints.ifInclusive: Present Christmas as one tradition among many, all equally special
decisionPoints.ifSensitive: Focus on cultural learning rather than religious aspects

materials: French Christmas tradition photos and videos
Simple craft materials for Christmas decoration
French Christmas carol recording and lyrics
Examples of different Christmas trees and decorations

whenThingsGoWrong.religiousSensitivity: Focus on cultural traditions rather than religious meanings
whenThingsGoWrong.studentExclusion: Emphasize learning about cultures, not personal belief
whenThingsGoWrong.craftDifficulty: Simplify to coloring or decorating pre-made items

lessons.closing: Students show their Christmas craft and say: 'Joyeux Noël!'
lessons.realWorldConnection: Christmas is celebrated differently around the world, including in French-speaking countries

lessons.title: Hanoukka - Festival des lumières
lessons.oneGoal: Students learn about Hanukkah as a winter celebration of lights
lessons.openingConnection: Noël has lumières! Another winter celebration with beautiful lumières is Hanoukka!

mainActivity.description: Hanukkah exploration with respectful cultural learning
activities: Introduce 'Hanoukka' with respect and celebration photos
Explore 'menorah' with nine-branched candleholder photos and counting
Learn 'huit' (eight) by counting eight nights and candles
Hanukkah story: simple story of lights lasting eight nights
Light counting activity: practice numbers with Hanukkah candles
Hanukkah craft: create simple paper menorah with eight candles
Hanukkah game: play simple dreidel-inspired spinning game with French numbers
visualSupports: Beautiful Hanukkah celebration photos showing families
Menorah photos and safe demonstration model
Number cards 1-8 for counting practice
Simple Hanukkah story picture book
Craft template for paper menorah

decisionPoints.question: Do students know about Jewish traditions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Build on existing knowledge with French vocabulary
decisionPoints.ifNo: Introduce gently as beautiful tradition of light and family

decisionPoints.question: Should I include hands-on menorah activity?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Create safe paper menorah craft for tactile learning
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on visual exploration and counting activities

decisionPoints.question: How can I teach respectfully about religious traditions?
decisionPoints.ifRespectfully: Present as cultural learning, emphasize beauty and family values
decisionPoints.ifCarefully: Focus on lights, numbers, and family celebration aspects

materials: Paper craft materials for menorah making

whenThingsGoWrong.religiousConcerns: Focus on cultural appreciation and family traditions
whenThingsGoWrong.conceptTooComplex: Simply focus on eight nights of lights and family celebration
whenThingsGoWrong.craftDifficulties: Provide pre-cut materials and simple assembly

lessons.closing: Students count to huit and point to their menorah craft
lessons.realWorldConnection: Hanukkah is an important winter festival celebrating religious freedom and miracles

lessons.title: Kwanzaa - Célébration africaine-américaine
lessons.oneGoal: Students discover Kwanzaa as a cultural winter celebration
lessons.openingConnection: Hanoukka has huit nights! Another winter célébration has sept special days: Kwanzaa!

mainActivity.description: Kwanzaa exploration with cultural appreciation and respect
activities: Introduce 'Kwanzaa' with cultural respect and celebration photos
Explore 'principes' (principles) as important family and community values
Learn 'sept' (seven) by counting seven days and seven principles
Kwanzaa colors: explore red, black, and green significance
Community values discussion: what makes communities strong?
Kwanzaa craft: create kinara (candleholder) with seven candles
Unity activity: practice working together as community value
visualSupports: Respectful Kwanzaa celebration photos
Kinara (candleholder) photos and demonstration model
Red, black, and green color displays
Community helper photos showing unity and cooperation
Number cards for counting to seven

decisionPoints.question: How can I present Kwanzaa respectfully?
decisionPoints.ifRespectfully: Focus on community values and family celebration aspects
decisionPoints.ifCarefully: Emphasize cultural appreciation and learning about African-American traditions

decisionPoints.question: Do students need background on African-American culture?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide simple, respectful context about African-American community celebrations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on universal values like unity, creativity, and responsibility

decisionPoints.question: Should I include the seven principles?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce simplified versions: unity, helping others, working together
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on sept days, couleurs, and family celebration

materials: Red, black, and green craft materials

whenThingsGoWrong.culturalMisunderstanding: Focus on universal values and respectful cultural learning
whenThingsGoWrong.tooComplicated: Simply focus on sept days of family celebration and community
whenThingsGoWrong.craftChallenges: Provide pre-made kinara template for decorating

lessons.closing: Students count sept candles and say one community value
lessons.realWorldConnection: Kwanzaa celebrates African-American culture and community values

lessons.title: Diwali d'hiver et autres fêtes
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore other cultural celebrations that can happen in winter
lessons.openingConnection: Winter has many lumières celebrations! Let's discover more beautiful traditions!

mainActivity.description: Diverse winter celebration exploration with inclusive cultural appreciation
activities: Introduce 'Diwali' as festival of lights (when it occurs in winter)
Explore 'lanternes' with beautiful lantern photos from different cultures
Learn 'tradition' as special ways families celebrate over time
Cultural light celebration tour: Chinese lanterns, Winter Solstice, Las Posadas
Light pattern exploration: compare different celebration lights and colors
Winter solstice simple explanation: longest night, celebrating light return
Create multicultural lantern craft representing different celebration traditions
visualSupports: Beautiful photos of lanterns from different cultures
Diwali celebration photos (if occurring in winter)
Winter solstice explanation with simple day/night visuals
Various cultural light celebration photos
Craft materials for simple lantern making

decisionPoints.question: Which other celebrations should I include?
decisionPoints.ifDiverse: Include Chinese New Year, Winter Solstice, Three Kings Day, Las Posadas
decisionPoints.ifFocused: Choose 2-3 celebrations represented in class or community

decisionPoints.question: Do students represent other cultures in class?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Invite students to share their family celebrations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Present celebrations as beautiful examples of world diversity

decisionPoints.question: Should I focus on light themes across cultures?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize how many cultures use lumières to celebrate in dark winter
decisionPoints.ifNo: Explore variety of celebration elements: food, music, family time

materials: Lantern craft materials (paper, tissue, safe lights)
Cultural music samples from different celebrations

whenThingsGoWrong.tooManyTraditions: Focus on 2-3 celebrations and explore them well
whenThingsGoWrong.culturalConfusion: Emphasize that all traditions are beautiful and meaningful
whenThingsGoWrong.craftComplexity: Simplify to decorating pre-made lantern shapes

lessons.closing: Students hold their lantern craft and name one winter tradition
lessons.realWorldConnection: Many cultures have light-based celebrations during dark winter months

lessons.title: Nouvel An autour du monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students discover different New Year celebrations and traditions
lessons.openingConnection: Many traditions in hiver! One special time is when we start a nouveau année!

mainActivity.description: New Year celebration exploration with hope and renewal themes
activities: Introduce 'nouveau' (new) with fresh, clean, beginning concepts
Explore 'année' (year) with calendar and time passage concepts
Learn 'souhaits' (wishes) with hoping and dreaming gestures
New Year around the world: January 1st, Chinese New Year, other cultural new years
New Year traditions comparison: fireworks, dragon dances, resolutions
Wish-making activity: students share hopes for nouveau année
Create New Year celebration noise makers with cultural decorations
visualSupports: New Year celebration photos from different cultures
Calendar showing different new year dates
Fireworks photos and dragon dance videos
Wish and hope gesture demonstrations
Noise maker craft materials

decisionPoints.question: Should I include lunar new year traditions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Show Chinese New Year dragon dances, red decorations, family traditions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on January 1st traditions and universal new year concepts

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand calendar concepts?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore different calendar systems and new year dates
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep simple with 'old year ends, new year begins' concept

decisionPoints.question: How can I make new year concepts age-appropriate?
decisionPoints.ifAge: Focus on hopes, family time, and celebration rather than resolutions
decisionPoints.ifSimple: Emphasize nouveau beginnings and family celebrating together

materials: Simple calendar for demonstrating year change
Wish cards or paper for hope activity

whenThingsGoWrong.timeConceptsConfusing: Focus on celebration and family gathering aspects
whenThingsGoWrong.wishesTooPersonal: Suggest simple wishes like kindness, fun, learning
whenThingsGoWrong.noiseMakersLoud: Create quiet versions or practice 'inside voices'

lessons.closing: Students shake their noise makers and shout: 'Bonne année!'
lessons.realWorldConnection: Different cultures celebrate new year at different times with unique traditions

lessons.title: Cuisine d'hiver réconfortante
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore comfort foods and special dishes from winter celebrations
lessons.openingConnection: Winter célébrations bring famille together! What special foods do families share?

mainActivity.description: Winter comfort food exploration with cultural food appreciation
activities: Introduce 'soupe' with warm, comfort food photos and steaming gestures
Explore 'chocolat' with hot chocolate photos and warm drink demonstrations
Learn 'biscuits' with holiday cookie photos and baking gesture
Cultural winter foods tour: matzo ball soup, hot chocolate, sugar cookies, latkes
Food and celebration matching: which foods go with which celebrations?
Sensory food exploration: smell spices, feel textures (safely)
Winter menu creation: students draw their favorite winter comfort foods
visualSupports: Diverse cultural winter food photos
Real food samples for safe smelling and observing
Cooking demonstration props (safe utensils, empty containers)
Cultural food-celebration matching cards
Seasonal spice bottles for safe sensory exploration

decisionPoints.question: Should I include cooking or tasting activities?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Prepare safe food samples considering allergies and dietary restrictions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on photos, smells, and visual food exploration

decisionPoints.question: Do students have food allergies to consider?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use only photos and sealed spice containers for sensory exploration
decisionPoints.ifNo: Include safe food samples and smelling activities

decisionPoints.question: Which cultural foods should I represent?
decisionPoints.ifDiverse: Include foods from Jewish, African-American, Latin, Asian, European traditions
decisionPoints.ifFocused: Choose foods that represent class cultural backgrounds

materials: Safe food samples or sealed containers

whenThingsGoWrong.allergyReactions: Remove all food immediately, use only photos
whenThingsGoWrong.culturalSensitivity: Present all cultural foods as equally delicious and special

lessons.closing: Students show their winter menu and name one comfort food
lessons.realWorldConnection: Special foods and warm drinks are important parts of winter celebrations

lessons.title: Musique et chansons d'hiver
lessons.oneGoal: Students learn songs and music from different winter celebrations
lessons.openingConnection: Winter foods warm our bodies! Winter musique and chansons warm our hearts!

mainActivity.description: Winter celebration music exploration with movement and cultural appreciation
activities: Introduce 'chanson' with singing gesture and diverse cultural songs
Explore 'musique' with musical instrument sounds and celebration music
Learn 'danser' with movement and cultural dance demonstrations
Cultural music tour: Christmas carols, Hanukkah songs, Kwanzaa music, folk songs
Instrument exploration: shakers, drums, bells from different celebrations
Movement activity: dance to different cultural celebration music
Create class winter celebration song combining elements from different cultures
visualSupports: Musical instruments from different cultures
Song lyric cards with picture supports
Cultural dance photos and videos
Music recording equipment for class song creation
Movement scarves and props for dancing

decisionPoints.question: Which songs are appropriate for this age?
decisionPoints.ifAge: Choose simple, repetitive songs with actions and familiar melodies
decisionPoints.ifCultural: Include songs from different traditions that are respectful and inclusive

decisionPoints.question: Should I include instruments or movement?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide simple instruments and encourage movement to music
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on singing and listening to different cultural music

decisionPoints.question: Do students need visual supports for song lyrics?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Create picture-supported lyric cards for each song
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on melody, rhythm, and movement rather than lyrics

whenThingsGoWrong.tooNoisy: Use quieter instruments or focus on humming and gentle movement
whenThingsGoWrong.reluctantParticipants: Allow listening and gentle swaying rather than full participation
whenThingsGoWrong.culturalMisrepresentation: Focus on appreciation and respect for all musical traditions

lessons.closing: Students choose their favorite winter song and hum together
lessons.realWorldConnection: Music and songs are essential parts of cultural celebrations

lessons.title: Créons nos décorations
lessons.oneGoal: Students create winter celebration decorations from different cultures
lessons.openingConnection: Beautiful musique for célébrations! Now let's créer beautiful décorations!

mainActivity.description: Multicultural decoration creation with artistic expression and cultural appreciation
activities: Introduce 'décorer' with decorating gesture and celebration decoration photos
Explore 'couleurs' with cultural color meanings: red/green Christmas, blue/white Hanukkah
Learn 'créer' with making and building gestures
Decoration station rotation: make ornaments, paper chains, cultural symbols
Cultural decoration exploration: stars, trees, menorahs, kinaras, lanterns
Classroom decoration project: create multicultural celebration display
Decoration sharing: students explain their creation and cultural inspiration

Cultural color meaning charts
Step-by-step craft instruction cards
Examples of finished decorations from each culture
Decoration station signs with pictures and instructions

decisionPoints.question: Do students need step-by-step craft support?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide visual instruction cards and demonstrate each step clearly
decisionPoints.ifNo: Allow creative exploration with minimal instruction

decisionPoints.question: Should I focus on one culture or multiple?
decisionPoints.ifOne: Choose one cultural decoration and make it well
decisionPoints.ifMultiple: Create stations representing different cultural decorations

materials: Craft supplies in cultural celebration colors

whenThingsGoWrong.craftFrustration: Provide simpler alternatives and focus on effort rather than perfection
whenThingsGoWrong.culturalInaccuracy: Focus on appreciation and creativity rather than authentic reproduction

lessons.closing: Students display their decorations and share cultural inspiration
lessons.realWorldConnection: People decorate their homes and communities for winter celebrations

lessons.title: Notre festival d'hiver multiculturel

lessons.openingConnection: We have food, musique, décorations! Time for our grand festival d'hiver!

mainActivity.description: Culminating multicultural winter festival celebration

Festival setup: arrange decorations, music stations, cultural displays

lessons.closing: Group circle celebrating diversity: 'Toutes les célébrations sont belles!'

lessons.title: Histoires d'hiver magiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore winter stories and legends from different cultures
lessons.openingConnection: Extension: Every culture has beautiful histoires about hiver! Let's discover magical winter stories!

Story sharing: students tell their winter story using French vocabulary
